title: A Machine-Checked Reduction of the Riemann Hypothesis to Pólya–Frequency Positivity of the ξ Taylor Coefficients
description:
Local revised manuscript, 10 October 2026; metadata preparation does not constitute a deposit or publication.

A Lean 4/Mathlib formalization of conditional reductions relating the Riemann Hypothesis to total nonnegativity of the sign-normalized xi coefficient Toeplitz matrix. No proof of RH is claimed. The classical equivalence is attributed to prior work, with ASW/Edrei, limit closure, Polya-Jensen and the converse carried as named hypotheses. The revised exposition distinguishes ordinary coefficients mu_n from the classical Jensen coefficients n! mu_n and separates full PF positivity from contiguous-minor extraction.

The paper gives the corrected entire xi target, explicit positive kernel normalization, moment determinant identities, a diagnostic quadratic lemma, and a separate pseudo-Hermitian eigenvector implication. FLINT/Arb certificates cover 121 positive coefficient balls, 119 strict log-concavity inequalities and 1816 positive contiguous minors of orders at most 16, using coefficients through index 120. These are finite consistency checks within classical positivity ranges, not uniform or RH proofs.

This revision adds a theorem/dependency ledger, exact Lean and Mathlib source pins, manifest and coefficient SHA-256 hashes, focused axiom audit source, replay instructions, regenerated figures and a paper-specific readiness checklist. Formal source pin: c749786972306bfe6be8890d78972bd9a2325f0c. Recent preprint claims remain external and unverified here. Author review and independent mathematical review remain necessary before submission.
